pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a xylophone, the long bars give (1 mark)
   A. no sound
   B. only clapping sounds
   C. high notes
   D. low notes

2. A gourd rattle makes sound because (1 mark)
   A. strings are plucked
   B. the seeds inside knock against the walls
   C. air is blown through it
   D. a bow is rubbed

3. Which is a non-melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Thumb piano
   B. Xylophone
   C. Marimba
   D. Shaker

4. In a drawing of a drum with light from the left, which part is darkest? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing is dark
   B. The white paper background always
   C. The side away from the light
   D. The side facing the light

5. In netball, the ball is moved mainly by (1 mark)
   A. running with it
   B. kicking it
   C. passing it
   D. rolling it

6. What is the correct way to catch a netball? (1 mark)
   A. With two hands, giving with the ball
   B. With your feet
   C. With your eyes closed
   D. With one hand held stiff

7. Which is an improvised glue? (1 mark)
   A. Engine oil
   B. Flour paste
   C. Paint thinner
   D. Salt water

8. After painting, how should you store a brush? (1 mark)
   A. Covered in paint
   B. Standing on its hairs in water
   C. Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   D. Under a heavy book

9. What is the theme of the montage in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Weather
   B. Ball games
   C. Food
   D. Wild animals

10. Which is a quality of a good rhythmic pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Variation of note values
   B. Ending on a rest always
   C. Only one kind of note
   D. No beat

11. How do you make a coil? (1 mark)
   A. Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   B. Bake it
   C. Beat it with a stick
   D. Cut it flat

12. What is patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Love of food
   B. Fear of runners
   C. Love for one's country
   D. A kind of race

13. Which foot is usually placed in front at the start? (1 mark)
   A. The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   B. Both together
   C. The weaker foot always
   D. Neither

14. In a partner check for the crab balance, how many touching points does the table have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. Six

15. Which quality do rolls and balances build? (1 mark)
   A. Colour mixing
   B. Balance and coordination
   C. Loud singing
   D. Reading speed

16. How long should you hold a crab balance in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Half a second
   B. Three to five counts
   C. Ten minutes
   D. One hour

17. If you finish a gymnastics session, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Push the mats
   B. Run around wildly
   C. Put equipment away and cool down
   D. Leave mats on the floor

18. Photos on a digital device are kept in its (1 mark)
   A. flash
   B. lens
   C. memory
   D. strap

19. Which of these makes a photograph too dark? (1 mark)
   A. A clean lens
   B. Too much practice
   C. Too little light
   D. A battery

20. To make the centre of interest clearer you can (1 mark)
   A. add lots of clutter
   B. move very far away
   C. shake the camera
   D. move closer to the subject

21. Before sharing a photograph of others, you should (1 mark)
   A. hide it
   B. edit their face
   C. ask them and an adult
   D. post it at once

22. If G is doh, then B is (1 mark)
   A. ray
   B. me
   C. soh
   D. doh

23. Which joint has the mouthpiece? (1 mark)
   A. Foot joint
   B. None
   C. Middle joint
   D. Head joint

24. A streamlined shape is (1 mark)
   A. round like a ball
   B. long and thin like an arrow
   C. bent like a chair
   D. wide and floppy

25. In the sit-and-slide entry, you should turn (1 mark)
   A. away from the wall
   B. upside down
   C. to the deep end
   D. to face the wall and hold the edge

26. What happens when the hawk tags the last chick? (1 mark)
   A. The chick becomes the hawk
   B. The game ends forever
   C. The hawk sleeps
   D. The hen goes home

27. Which is a rule for animal games? (1 mark)
   A. Do not push, trip or pull others
   B. Push others to go faster
   C. Play without looking
   D. Ignore the whistle

28. How are indigenous games mostly learnt? (1 mark)
   A. By reading long books only
   B. By watching and joining in
   C. By buying kits
   D. By watching TV only

29. The crab walk is done (1 mark)
   A. on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   B. standing tall
   C. face down on the tummy
   D. lying still

30. A display portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. your best finished works
   B. tools
   C. only rubbish
   D. only rough drafts

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how to compose a short melody using d, r and m. (4 marks)

32. Name the three primary colours. (2 marks)

33. Give one example of a melodic percussion instrument and one non-melodic percussion instrument. (2 marks)

34. How can an elder help you to learn indigenous games? (2 marks)

35. State the lengths of a crotchet rest and a quaver rest and how to show a rest when clapping. (3 marks)

36. Describe how you would enter the pool and perform a glide safely. (5 marks)

37. Why is colour classification important in painting? (2 marks)

38. Name two animal movement games. (2 marks)

39. Describe how to compose a short melody with d, r and m, and how to check that it is a good melody. (5 marks)

40. Give three ways of storing and handling a recorder safely. (3 marks)

41. Describe three qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. (3 marks)

42. Why should a composed rhythm be your own idea? (2 marks)

43. Explain how to analyse a folk song performance using its components. (5 marks)

44. Explain where the sun should be when you photograph a person and why. (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between the prone float and the supine float. (3 marks)

46. State four rules for playing the hawk and the chicks game. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — low notes
   Longer bars vibrate more slowly and sound lower.

2. B — the seeds inside knock against the walls
   When shaken, seeds inside hit the gourd and make a sound.

3. D — Shaker
   A shaker gives a rattling sound but not different notes for a tune.

4. C — The side away from the light
   Shadows fall on the side away from the light, so it is darker.

5. C — passing it
   Players may not run with the ball, so they pass it to move it forward.

6. A — With two hands, giving with the ball
   A double-handed catch with elbows bending as the ball arrives is correct.

7. B — Flour paste
   Flour mixed with water and heated water makes a paste.

8. C — Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   Washing and shaping the tip keeps the brush in good shape.

9. B — Ball games
   The montage is themed ball games.

10. A — Variation of note values
   Good patterns vary the note values.

11. A — Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   Rolling back and forth makes a long even coil.

12. C — Love for one's country
   Patriotism is love and respect for one's country.

13. A — The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   The stronger foot is the front foot.

14. C — Four
   The table has four legs, two hands and two feet.

15. B — Balance and coordination
   Gymnastics teaches the body to stay steady and move parts together.

16. B — Three to five counts
   Hold the balance for three to five slow counts.

17. C — Put equipment away and cool down
   Tidying and cooling down are good habits.

18. C — memory
   Digital photos are stored in memory.

19. C — Too little light
   Poor light makes dark pictures.

20. D — move closer to the subject
   Getting closer helps the subject fill the picture.

21. C — ask them and an adult
   Respect and safety come first.

22. B — me
   G, A, B match d, r, m.

23. D — Head joint
   The mouthpiece is at the top of the head joint.

24. B — long and thin like an arrow
   A long shape slips easily through water.

25. D — to face the wall and hold the edge
   You hold the edge as you lower yourself in.

26. A — The chick becomes the hawk
   Roles change so everyone plays.

27. A — Do not push, trip or pull others
   Safety comes first.

28. B — By watching and joining in
   Elders and children play together.

29. A — on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   It is like the crab balance, but moving.

30. A — your best finished works
   It is for showing to others.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give a syllable to each note. Use steps. End on d as a crotchet. Sing it and show the hand signs. Write the syllables under the rhythm names.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Red, yellow and blue.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for all three, 1 mark for two.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Melodic: xylophone. Non-melodic: shaker, kayamba or claves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: The elder can teach you the games and songs of the community and share their stories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet rest is one beat of silence and a quaver rest is half a beat of silence. When clapping, we do not clap but keep the beat silently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each length, 1 mark for showing the rest.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Get permission and warm up. Enter feet first by the steps or sit and slide. Stay in shallow water. Stand with the back to the wall and stretch the arms overhead. Put feet on the wall, breathe, put the face in, push off gently and glide with a straight body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five parts.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us know which colours to mix to get others. It shows that only primary colours are needed to make all the other colours.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Frog jump, crab walk, elephant walk, snake slither, hare hop, crocodile crawl, giraffe stretch, monkey swing. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give each note a syllable, using steps. End on d. Sing it with hand signs. Check that it has variation and stepwise motion and that it ends on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five valid points.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it in a bag or case; keep away from heat; do not drop it; twist joints gently; do not bite it. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has variation of note values, repetition of a group of notes and ends on a long note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Copying is not fair and honest. Your own idea shows integrity and creativity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Say the community of origin, the type or occasion, the message and mood, the roles of the soloist, chorus and instrumentalists, and the instruments used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five components.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind the photographer, so light falls on the front of the person. If the sun is behind the subject, the face is in shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 2 marks for the reason.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prone is face down in the water with arms stretched forward. Supine is on the back with the face up and ears in the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each float, 1 mark for the difference.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold but do not pull; the hawk tags gently; no pushing or tripping; stop at the whistle; take turns. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
